lens: Read this cold as a sceptical nucleic-acid-therapeutics referee with no stake in the result. Attack the framing of the two named gapmers, the boundedness of every selectivity and liability statement, whether an in-silico screen can support the conclusion drawn from it, whether the paper's own limitations section names the limitations a referee would name, and whether anything in the abstract or discussion would let a reader believe more was demonstrated than was. You are not looking for arithmetic errors; you are looking for the sentence you would quote in a rejection.
central_claim: Two 16-mer 5-6-5 gapmers, at the two most-reported NR4A3 fusion breakpoints, come through a five-part in-silico specificity screen with no wild-type parent pairing their whole catalytic gap at the paper's ten-base-pair criterion, and are named — with two screened scramble controls and a pre-registrable selectivity cut — as the reagents a laboratory should synthesise, against a panel finding that 87 of 190 junction designs fail exactly that parent test.

p1s.summary: The genome-wide screen's exact-match stratum is omitted from the article, and it is the stratum in which one NAMED reagent carries a perfect 16/16, strand-agreeing, gap-fully-paired site inside an annotated lncRNA. The article reports only the raw <=2-mismatch count it then discounts, and its discounting rationale ('most of it never transcribed') does not reach that site.
p1s.evidence: Re-derived from research/modalities/aso-genome-offtarget.json. The article's only genome sentence is 'The genome-wide screen does not separate them: 156 hybridisable gap-paired sites against 135' (line 162); I confirm counts.hybridisable_gap_paired_le2 = 156 (GGGCATATCATCAAAC) and 135 (GGGCATATCTTGTGTG). The same artifact's per_design block gives, for the EWSR1 reagent, counts.exact = 1 and one exact_site: chr3:176354948-176354963, orientation sense, mismatches 0, gap_mismatches 0, gap_fully_paired true, hybridisable true, genes ['ENSG00000304430'], biotypes ['lncRNA'], compartment intronic, softmask_fraction 0.0. The TAF15 reagent has counts.exact = 0. Panel-wide I counted 236 exact sites over 97 of 176 designs, of which 93 are hybridisable AND gap-fully-paired, spread over 58 designs (44 protein-coding intronic, 38 lncRNA intronic, 7 lncRNA exonic, 4 protein-coding exonic). The producing artifact's own headline calls this 'the four strata below are what this screen can actually say' and names stratum 1 'the class the core_nt arm could never reach'. The companion research article DOES report it and adds the warning the journal article lacks — 'a reagent should be read from its own row rather than from the mean' (fusion-junction-aso-research-article.md:950-955). Neither the journal article nor its SI contains the words 'exact', '16/16' or 'lncRNA' in this sense (grepped). The asymmetry is the tell: the article discloses a WEAKER site for the same molecule — the two-mismatch TAF15 precursor hit, which I confirmed at aso-premrna-offtarget.json per_design (mismatches 2, gap_mismatches 1, gap_fully_paired false) — while omitting the zero-mismatch one. Note in fairness that 1 exact site is AT chance (artifact's expected_per_design = 1.37305, o/e = 0.7283), so this is an omission of a per-reagent reading, not evidence of an excess.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Nothing in the repository binds the article's genome paragraph to the strata the artifact computes. A future re-run of aso_genome_offtarget.py that moves the exact site (a new assembly patch, a changed annotation release, or a different softmask reference) would silently change which named reagent carries one, and the article would read identically either way. Conversely, if this finding is fixed by adding one sentence naming the site, that sentence is bound to nothing: adding a design, changing MAX_MISMATCHES, or restricting the scan would leave the sentence in place and stale. Any repair should read the count out of aso-genome-offtarget.json['per_design'][*]['counts']['exact'] rather than typing it.

p1s.summary: Every screen the paper rests on is substitution-only — no insertion, deletion or bulged duplex is searched anywhere — and the article states that bound for exactly one of the five screens and never names it in the Limitations. The energy re-scoring additionally DISCARDS gapped alignments, and the article does not say so.
p1s.evidence: Article line 114 states the bound only for screen 2: 'complete for substitutions within a one-mismatch budget'. Grepping the whole article for 'insertion|deletion|bulge|indel|gapped' returns that line and nothing else; the three-limit Limitations paragraph (line 366) names cleavage-vs-hybridisation, nil method novelty and delivery, and does not name search-space shape. Re-derived from the producing code and artifacts: aso-premrna-offtarget.json['method']['blind_to'] lists 'insertions and deletions' explicitly; aso-genome-offtarget.json['method']['algorithm'] is 'the complete <=2-substitution neighbourhood' (substitution-only by construction); aso_parent_gap_pairing.py compares ungapped 16-nt windows, so it cannot represent a bulge; aso-offtarget-duplex-energy.json['method']['records_not_scored'] begins 'gapped alignments', and its summary carries n_records_unscorable = 110 of 23331. The companion research article states the generalisation the journal article does not: 'screens 2 to 5 ... are substitution-only by construction' and '110 retained alignments carry an indel and 28 of those are counted as gap-paired sense-strand matches' (fusion-junction-aso-research-article.md:2289-2295). So every number the article reports as a liability count — 87, 19, 93, 8, 45, 123 against 8, 156 against 135 — is bounded by a search shape the reader is never told about, and the 8/45 energy classes are computed after 110 records were dropped.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: This is an omission, so nothing regresses it — but a repair is fragile in the same way. A sentence saying 'all five screens are substitution-only' would be silently falsified if the alignment arm's counts were ever taken directly from blastn (which returns gapped alignments and, per the companion article, already retains 110 of them) rather than through the energy module that drops them. Any fix should say which arms are substitution-only BY CONSTRUCTION (2, 3, 4, 5) and that arm 1's gapped hits are dropped at re-scoring, matching aso-offtarget-duplex-energy.json['summary']['n_records_unscorable'].

p1s.summary: The gap-length paragraph's headline invariance — 'the liable count holds at 87, 88 and 87' — is an artifact of a threshold that does not scale with the gap, and the producing artifact says in terms that the other reading must be reported alongside it. Under the geometry-invariant criterion the liability falls from 181 designs to 130 to 87, a four-fold drop in rate that would weaken the paper's own negative and is not shown.
p1s.evidence: Re-derived from research/modalities/aso-gap-length-tradeoff.json['geometries']. The three geometries' mature_parent_whole_gap_duplex blocks give n_at_or_above_min_duplex_bp = 87, 88, 87 over 190, 266, 342 designs (45.79%, 33.08%, 25.44% — the article's 45.8/33.1/25.4, confirmed). The SAME blocks give n_with_any_gap_pairing_window = 181, 130, 87, i.e. 95.3%, 48.9%, 25.4% under 'can a wild-type parent pair the whole catalytic gap at all', which is the criterion whose meaning does not change with gap length. The artifact's own _geometry._note says: 'MIN_DUPLEX_BP is an ABSOLUTE hybrid length and does NOT scale with the gap ... at a gap of 10 the catalytic gap alone is already a 10 bp hybrid, so every gap-pairing window clears the threshold by construction ... at a gap of 6 a window needs four further flanking pairs to reach it. Both readings are real and they are not the same reading, so compare geometries on the raw longest_parent_duplex_bp_through_gap distribution as well.' The article carries half of that caveat — it says the 5-10-5 figure 'is a floor' — but not the half that matters for the comparison: at 5-6-5 the criterion is gap + 4 flanking pairs and at 5-10-5 it is gap + 0, so the constancy of 87/88/87 compares three different stringencies. The direction of the omission flatters the paper's claim, since 'Lengthening the catalytic gap does not remove this liability' reads as invariance and the uniform reading shows a four-fold reduction.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: aso_gap_length_tradeoff.py imports MIN_DUPLEX_BP from aso_parent_gap_pairing rather than typing it, so a future change to the 10-bp criterion would move all three counts together and the article's '87, 88 and 87' would go stale with no gate firing on it — the three numbers are typed in prose and bound to nothing. A repair that adds the 181/130/87 series has the same exposure and should be generated, not typed.

p1s.summary: The pre-registered primary endpoint is a ratio whose denominator the paper never establishes is measurable in any test article it names. Selectivity is defined as wild-type NR4A3 over fusion 'in the same wells', but three of the five named test articles are heterologously over-expressed fusion cDNAs whose recipient background is never named and whose wild-type NR4A3 expression is never stated, and the two articles that unambiguously carry a wild-type allele are at the wrong acceptor.
p1s.evidence: Article line 319: 'Selectivity is the ratio of two half-maximal knockdown concentrations: wild-type NR4A3 over the fusion, from a matched dose-response in the same wells.' Grepping the article for 'wild-type NR4A3' returns only the Discussion's screen sentences and 'the patient's own un-rearranged NR4A3 allele' at line 354, which is about a search compartment and not about a test article; grepping for 'endogenous', 'recipient', 'tBJ', 'retroviral' returns only line 264's caveat about the fusion arm. The three engineered articles are verbatim cDNA constructs — research/modalities/emc-test-article-routes.json, route R3, construct_spec_verbatim from PMC6766969: 'The following cDNAs, cloned into the retroviral PLPCX vector ... E-N, corresponding to EWSR1 (exons 1-12)-NR4A3 (exons 3-8) ... T-N*, corresponding to the commonest TAF15 (exons 1-6)-NR4A3 (exons 3-8)'; the same artifact records the background only as 'tBJ/ER ... maintained and engineered by retroviral infections as described', a detail the article does not carry. The article's stated caveat covers the numerator only — 'a heterologously over-expressed complementary DNA speaks to junction-selective knockdown of the intended transcript, not to activity at an endogenous locus' (line 263-264) — and says nothing about whether the ratio's wild-type arm exists in those cells. The two patient-derived models that certainly carry an un-rearranged allele are at NR4A3 exon 2 (research/modalities/emc-model-junction-evidence.json, both models, verbatim from PMC9813045), which the article itself says is not this panel's acceptor. So the experiment the paper offers as its falsification route may have no article in which its own endpoint is defined.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: aso_falsification_power.py binds CUT and SIGMA and derives the four power/void figures (I re-ran it from a scratch copy: n=3 power 30.42%, n=6 81.28%; void_sd 0.648/1.534/2.250 — the article's 30%/80% and 0.65/1.53/2.25, confirmed), but nothing in the repository binds the ENDPOINT DEFINITION to the test-article list. Editing either section alone leaves the other consistent-looking: a future change of test article, or of the acceptor the panel designs against, would not disturb the ratio sentence, and re-pinning the cut would not disturb the test-article section.

p2s.summary: The abstract compresses the scope statement in the flattering direction: 'executing an industry off-target framework's in-silico step' drops the qualifier the Methods carry, which is that step 1 of five pairs complementarity prediction WITH transcriptomics analysis and only the complementarity half was performed.
p2s.evidence: Abstract line 45 against Methods line 94: 'set five steps; only the first is even partly in silico, pairing complementarity prediction with transcriptomics. This work performs the in-silico half of the first step and stops there.' The source's own enumeration is held verbatim at research/manuscripts/aso/lit-targets-aso-instruments.json: 'The proposed workflow encompasses five key steps: (1) OffT identification through complementarity prediction and transcriptomics analysis ...' (PMID 39912803, confirmed as 'Assessing Hybridization-Dependent Off-Target Risk for Therapeutic Oligonucleotides: Updated Industry Recommendations', Nucleic Acid Ther 35:16-33, in fusion-junction-aso-journal-references.md:64). Transcriptomics analysis is itself in silico, so 'the in-silico step' names both halves while the journal article delivers one — the companion research article carries an off-target expression arm (Table 6), the journal article does not.
p2s.what_edit_would_break_it: The instruments artifact records that a named test forbids 'all five', 'the first three steps' and 'steps one to' at the Methods sentence, but that guard is bound to the Methods line only. The abstract's compressed wording sits outside it, so tightening or loosening the abstract cannot fail any gate.

p2s.summary: 'All five junctions with a published exon-resolved breakpoint have one' is scoped to the 38-junction panel but does not say so, and the paper itself names a sixth published exon-resolved breakpoint that the panel excludes — so the default reading overstates how much of the published breakpoint set is covered.
p2s.evidence: Line 227, in a sentence whose subject is 'the 38 junctions'. Re-derived from research/modalities/aso-parent-gap-pairing.json: 35 of 38 junctions have a design with counts_as_liability false, and all five of aso-parent-null.json's cut_sensitivity.published_breakpoint_junctions (EWSR1_e12, EWSR1_e13, TAF15_e6, TCF12_e5, TFG_e7, all to NR4A3_e3) clear at the 10-bp cut — both figures confirmed. But research/manuscripts/aso/lit-targets-aso-breakpoint-census.json['junction_census'] carries EWSR1_e7__NR4A3_e2 at k=1/n=20 with three sources (PMID 29937513 sequenced, 22567356, 35488288), and the article itself states that junction at line 254-256. It is a published exon-resolved breakpoint with no design in the panel, so 'all five' is five-of-six at least, counted over the literature rather than over the panel. The article corrects this two sections later at length; a referee reading Results linearly does not have it yet.
p2s.what_edit_would_break_it: The five-junction list lives in aso-parent-null.json['cut_sensitivity']['published_breakpoint_junctions'] and the census lives in a different file with a different denominator; nothing cross-checks them. Adding an exon-2 junction to the panel would change 38 and 35 without touching the word 'five', and adding a newly sequenced breakpoint to the census would not touch the article at all.
